newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* European leaders moved ahead with plans for a single currency after dismissing French contentions that the priority should be the reduction of unemployment rather than budget deficits.
* Buoyed by the popularity of large utility and four-wheel-drive vehicles, American car makers are about to push out even larger models that come with large sticker prices.
* Efforts to keep liquor ads off TV have been dealt a setback after a member of the Federal Communications Commission asked that an investigation into the ads be delayed for at least a month.
* Stocks offered mixed results Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrials average shaved by 9.95 points, closing at 7772.09, but the Nasdaq rising 8.92 points to 1431.95.
* McLeodUSA has agreed to acquire rival telecommunications company Consolidated Communications Inc for $400 million in cash and stock.

* Louis Navellier, who was ousted earlier this year as manager of the Navellier Aggressive Small Cap Equity Fund, may have opened the door to regaining control of the fund by seeking to block an effort by its trustees to award Massachusetts Financial Services a management contract.
* KeyCorp has agreed to acquire Champion Mortgage Co Inc, a home equity finance company, for $200 million in stock.
* Kmart Corp, looking to concentrate on running its business in the United States, has sold its 123-store Kmart Canada unit for $134 million.
* Foreign mining companies are eyeing Congo, seeking the chance to extract the country's mineral riches.
* Eastman Kodak Co is switching advertising firms for its consumer imaging business to Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide, dropping its long-standing ad agency J. Walter Thompson.
* The California Public Employees' Retirement System unveiled a set of proposed governance guidelines for U.S. companies in its $113 billion portfolio.
* Genesis Health Ventures Inc has agreed to acquire Multicare Cos Inc for $1.06 billion in cash.
* Real estate investment trusts are on a shopping spree, and their most frequent object of desire these days are office buildings.
